the role of SCFA butyrate in the regulation of T cell-mediated immune response and its impact on the development of colitis.
the mechanisms by which the bacterial metabolite butyrate regulates the differentiation of CD4+ effector T cells and the generation of regulatory T cells.

butyrate is a potent immunomodulator, which is able to induce both immunosuppressive and immunogenic effects.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
butyrate at physiological concentrations promotes Treg differentiation and suppresses inflammatory responses in vivo and in vitro.
SCFA butyrate, at concentrations that occur in the gut, may promote the generation of Treg cells.
butyrate is a double-edged sword that can either promote or inhibit T cell-mediated immunity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the beneficial effects of butyrate are limited to its physiological concentrations in the millimolar ranges.
